evidence: The manifest is candid: it claims only GENERATED and PARTIAL, requires independent validation, and sets productionized to false; no BUILDS, TESTED, FUZZED, BENCHMARKED, REVIEWED, TRANSFER_VERIFIED, or PRODUCTIONIZED claim was found.

The learner material is coherent and useful: the specification is normative, starter TODOs are explicit, public tests are labeled incomplete, and later debugging/review/adversarial/benchmark material is progressively staged.

Independent view reconstruction reproduced core/debugging/review/adversarial/benchmarks counts 25/29/33/34/35 and the submitted SHA-256 identities; no reconstructed view contained sealed or administrator-only metadata.
A locally materialized core view contained exactly 25 regular files and no sealed, later-stage, provenance, license-boundary, or validation root.

Manifest, provenance, and license-boundary records consistently distinguish the CC0 catalog snapshot from the linked resource whose license is NOASSERTION; generated material grants no redistribution right beyond the stated personal educational use.

The evaluator boundary is not a reliable isolation control: legal ECMAScript comments defeat its import regexes, candidate and oracle execute in one process with shared globals, and candidate-defined error classes are used to decide whether candidate errors have the expected class.

The reference VM's prevalidation checks object and operand shapes but performs stack underflow and final-height checks only during dispatch, contrary to the starter/design promise that stack use is validated before execution.

Recursive parser, evaluator, and compiler paths have no nesting limit or host-stack containment, so deeply nested valid or malformed inputs can leak a host RangeError instead of the documented Pebble error boundary; the candidate's own sealed review accurately discloses this risk.
Python-side structural results are reproducible, but there is no independent JavaScript syntax, module-load, reference-test, differential, fuzz, timing, or benchmark result.
limitations: No Node.js-compatible runtime, npm, or JavaScript parser library was available, so JavaScript execution and syntax acceptance remain unverified.

The source catalog checkout and linked upstream repository were outside the readable review workspace; provenance assertions and the no-copy claim could be checked for internal consistency but not independently compared with source content or license evidence.
